target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define 'Self-directed households' as the total number of households that include at least one active account with self-directed assets. The definition is consistent across years.

Both disclosures address the counting methodology for households/participants across Wealth Management channels, specifically noting that individuals engaged in multiple channels are included in each respective channel count. The 2023 disclosure (D056) includes this in sentence S002, and the 2024 disclosure (D054) contains it as the primary definition in S001.

comparisons.peer_summary: Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank, with Merrill focused on clients with over $250,000 in assets and both units serving high net worth clients.
comparisons.comparison: Both firms define the composition of their wealth management businesses and the client segments served. MS specifies the accounting methodology for counting households engaged in multiple channels, whereas BAC outlines the structural separation of its wealth management into distinct businesses with different asset thresholds. MS counts individuals engaged in 'one or more' channels in each respective count, while BAC distinguishes between Merrill Wealth Management (focused on clients with over $250,000 in assets) and Bank of America Private Bank (targeting high net worth clients).

sentences.text: Individual households or participants that are engaged in one or more of our Wealth Management channels are included in each of the respective channel counts.
GWIM consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank.
